assessments.reasoning: October 2021 §3.3.1 requires the query root to be present and an Object. Mutation and subscription roots are optional but are distinct Object types when supplied. Default Root Operation Type Names can admit an omitted schema block while still providing a query root.

challenge.method: Tested explicit missing root, scalar or interface root, default Query object inferred in an omitted schema block, and optional mutation roots by reading §3.3.1.
challenge.results: An absent query root or non-Object fails; an inferred Object named Query can satisfy the requirement. Mutation or subscription absence does not contradict the statement.

limitations: A schema declaration block can be omitted when default root naming applies. Mutation and subscription roots are optional and must be object types when supplied.
The assessment is confined to the named documents and revision scope.
